nodes.name: Founder v1
nodes.summary: A voice-first agent that learns repeatable company workflows from successful attempts.

attempts.title: Frame the wedge
attempts.result: Selected high-friction operational tasks as the initial market.

fileChanges.summary: Created the initial market and product thesis.

conversations.summary: Teams want proof, control, and an audit trail before autonomy.

lessons: Trust is a product surface, not a compliance appendix.
Branch histories make agent learning legible.

nodes.name: Healthcare
nodes.summary: Test whether auditability and confirmation gates create a strong healthcare wedge.

attempts.title: Map hospital workflows
attempts.result: Prior authorization and scheduling ranked highest on pain and repetition.

fileChanges.summary: Added buyer map, risks, and workflow shortlist.

conversations.summary: Procurement needs an exportable action log and strict approval boundaries.

lessons: Audit history resonates immediately, but procurement is slow.

nodes.name: Enterprise Pricing
nodes.summary: Package governance, audit logs, and reusable runbooks as an enterprise control plane.

attempts.title: Price anchoring
attempts.result: $60k pilot anchored well against one contractor headcount.

fileChanges.summary: Replaced usage pricing with annual platform tiers.

conversations.summary: Asked for fixed cost, deployment limits, and an exit clause.

lessons: Sell predictable control, not token consumption.

nodes.name: Hospital Sales
nodes.summary: Lead with a narrow scheduling workflow and a visible safety boundary.

attempts.title: Cold outbound
attempts.result: Compliance language earned opens but few meetings.

fileChanges.summary: Tested a five-touch hospital operations sequence.

emails.subject: A safer way to automate scheduling

lessons: Compliance earns attention but not urgency; lead with the workflow outcome.

nodes.name: Developers
nodes.summary: Turn trajectory capture and replay into a developer-native agent debugging product.

attempts.title: Developer positioning
attempts.result: Version history outperformed generic observability in five interviews.

fileChanges.summary: Defined local-first workflow, personas, and wedge.

conversations.summary: Asked for a diff between two successful trajectories.

lessons: Developers already think in branches, diffs, and replays.

nodes.name: Open Source
nodes.summary: Open the trajectory format and keep hosted collaboration as the paid layer.

attempts.title: README launch
attempts.result: A concrete trace example drove repository saves.

fileChanges.summary: Added a five-minute quickstart and trace screenshot.

conversations.summary: Requested adapters for LangGraph and CrewAI.

lessons: The artifact format is the adoption surface; integrations create pull.

nodes.name: CLI
nodes.summary: Make branching, inspection, and replay feel like a familiar source-control loop.

attempts.title: Command prototype
attempts.result: Users completed first branch inspection without documentation.

fileChanges.summary: Implemented tree, inspect, and diff commands.

conversations.summary: Four expected keyboard navigation and one asked for JSON output.

lessons: Tree, inspect, and diff are enough for the first developer loop.

nodes.name: Marketing
nodes.summary: Test whether visible agent branching can create a shareable product story.

attempts.title: Message matrix
attempts.result: ‘See every decision’ beat ‘autonomous workflows’ on clarity.

fileChanges.summary: Compared autonomy, learning, and auditability narratives.

emails.subject: Pitch: Git history for agent work

conversations.summary: Recommended showing a visual branch story before explaining architecture.

lessons: The branch picture explains the product faster than the phrase ‘agent memory.’

nodes.name: TikTok
nodes.summary: Show three agents trying visibly different paths in a 25-second split-screen narrative.

attempts.title: Three-hook test
attempts.result: The ‘watch agents disagree’ hook retained viewers longest.

fileChanges.summary: Captured hooks, storyboard, and disclosure language.

conversations.summary: Asked for raw screen capture and a visible spend counter.

lessons: Conflict is the hook; the learned runbook is the payoff.

nodes.name: Google Ads
nodes.summary: Bid on agent observability and debugging intent with audit-history landing copy.

attempts.title: Search campaign
attempts.result: Clicks were expensive and mostly research-stage.

fileChanges.summary: Logged keyword groups, copy, bids, and outcomes.

conversations.summary: Both wanted general monitoring rather than branch replay.

lessons: Search demand is broad and expensive before the category is understood.
